question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{{t}^{2}+t-6}{{t}^{2}-9t+14} & =\frac{{2}^{2}+2-6}{{2}^{2}-9(2)+14}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{t}^{2}+t-6}{{t}^{2}-9t+14} & =\frac{(t+3)(t-2)}{(t-2)(t-7)} \\  & =\frac{t+3}{t-7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 2}\frac{{t}^{2}+t-6}{{t}^{2}-9t+14} & ={lim}_{t\to 2}\frac{t+3}{t-7} \\  & =\frac{2+3}{2-7} \\  & =\frac{5}{(-5)} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
